paragraphs.text: Hide, reorder or show each button under an assistant reply in DeepSeek Harness
# dsh-chat-actions
中文说明

Show or hide each button that sits under every assistant reply in DeepSeek Harness, and keep the
hid
den ones one click away behind a single `⋯`.
## The buttons
The settings page lists exactly the buttons a rendered reply carries: open one assistant answer and

the page grows a switch per button it has. The shipped four keep the wording above; anything else
(a

nother plugin's button, one you added by hand) is listed under its own name. No switch exists for
a

button that is not on screen, and no button is listed twice — the usage chip, for instance, has a
te
xt label of its own, so it shows up once under that name instead of as a second 「用量」.

Drag a switch row to set where that item sits in the row: the order is saved as dragged and
applies

to every reply. The time stamp is an item too — it cannot be clicked, but it can be hidden
and moved

The time stamp is an item too — it cannot be clicked, but it can be hidden
and moved like the rest.
The copy button on a code block belongs to the editor, not to this row, and is never touched.
The first switch on the settings page, on by default:
- **on** — hidden buttons leave the row and reappear in a small popover under a `⋯` button. Hovering

a revealed button still shows its label: the shipped bubble when the popover opens downwards, and
t

he same text drawn above the icon when it opens upwards (the last reply sits on the composer, so
the

popover has to flip) — that way the popover can sit right next to the `⋯`.
- **off** — hidden butto

ns are simply gone.
- The switch is disabled while every button is visible: there is nothing to coll

ect, and no `⋯`
renders in the chat in that state.

Settings live in its own section of the settings drawer: 设置 → dsh-chat-actions. State is stored in
`

$DSH_HOME/dsh-chat-actions.json` (`~/.dsh/dsh-chat-actions.json` by default), not in
`localStorage`,

because the Web GUI picks a new port on every launch and per-origin storage would not
survive a res

use the Web GUI picks a new port on every launch and per-origin storage would not
survive a restart.
## Install
Needs a DeepSeek Harness build that loads plugin bundles (`dsh.bundle` in `package.json`).
From an agent session in this folder:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Harness links the folder into the active profile (`link:` in the profile `package.json`), so it keep

s
tracking this source tree instead of a copy. After that it shows up as a bundle in 插件 and adds its

source tree instead of a copy. After that it shows up as a bundle in 插件 and adds its
section to 设置.
Edits and restarts:

- `client.js` and `locale/*` are re-read on every page load — refresh the GUI (⌘R / Ctrl+R).
- `inde

x.js` is the host half and only runs when the plugin starts — toggle the bundle off and on
(`plugin_

manager action=set_bundle target=dsh-chat-actions enabled=false`, then `enabled=true`), or
restart H

action=set_bundle target=dsh-chat-actions enabled=false`, then `enabled=true`), or
restart Harness.
Remove it with `plugin_manager action=remove_bundle target=dsh-chat-actions`, or from the 插件 page.
## Test
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`tests/self-check.mjs` stubs the module loader and `fetch`, then asserts the generated stylesheet
(o

ne hide rule per switched-off button, the `⋯` reveal rules with their cell offsets), `sanitize()`
dr
opping unknown keys, and the slot registrations.
## Limits

- Buttons are found by name first (`aria-label`, then `title`, then text) and tagged with
`data-dca-

key`; the stylesheet only ever matches that attribute, so extra or reordered buttons
cannot shift wh

at a switch hides. Only a nameless icon button falls back to its position (first
and last direct but

ton, the only dialog trigger, the first two feedback buttons) — the `shortcut:`
comment in `client.j

s` marks that fallback.
- Tagging runs in the mutation callback before the stylesheet is written, so

a new button does not
flash visible first; the settings page only lists a switch after a reply has

rendered (before that
it shows a one-line hint).
- Digits in a live label are folded (`Usage 129K to

k` → `Usage #K tok`), so a changing counter cannot
mint switches; the cost is that two buttons whose

names differ only in digits, or two with the same
name, share one switch.
- A key stays in `extra`

in `$DSH_HOME/dsh-chat-actions.json` after its button stops appearing (up to
24 of them), but it pro

duces no row, because rows come from what is rendered.
- The `⋯` popover is placed with measured coo

rdinates (24px cells, 32px card); a cell clips text and
keeps the icon, and the name shows on hover.
- Sorting only flattens a **direct** wrapper. The usage chip sits in its own box, and the shipped u

sage
popover measures that box, so it keeps its layout: `order` goes on the wrapper that is the real

flex
item (`data-dca-slot`), not on the button.
- A button with a popover of its own (the usage chi

p) is never collected: switching it off just hides
it. The shipped popover measures the chip's own b

ox, so once that box is parked in a `⋯` cell the
popover can only land in the corner.
- The usage ch

ip and the stamp share one wrapper, so sorting treats the pair as one item: whichever
of the two com
es first in the order moves it.
